rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protection Ordinance - Just Cause Eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords in San Diego must have a legally recognized 'just cause' reason (at-fault or no-fault) to terminate most residential tenancies, must provide specific notice requirements, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.key_value: 2 months rent (3 months if senior/disabled) relocation assistance
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenancies in San Diego of more than 30 days, excluding numerous categories listed (hotels, transient occupancy, deed-restricted affordable housing without Section 8 voucher exclusion, mobilehomes under MRL, nonprofit/institutional housing, shared facilities with owner, small owner-occupied properties, certain individually-owned units with notice, and housing issued certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years).
rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; short-term occupancy ≤30 days; deed-restricted affordable housing (except Section 8 voucher holders); mobilehomes subject to MRL; nonprofit hospital/religious/elder care/transitional housing; dormitories; owner-occupied shared bathroom/kitchen; single-family owner-occupied with ≤2 units/bedrooms rented; duplex with owner occupying one unit; individually-owned condo/unit meeting non-corporate ownership and notice requirements; housing issued certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years.
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§ 98.0700 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2, to limit the reasons for termination of a residential tenancy, to require greater tenant relocation assistance in specified circumstances and to provide additional tenant protections.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing, or individually owned by a non-corporate owner with notice of exemption

rules.conflict_note: The ordinance incorporates notice requirements under CC 1946.1/1946.2 but adds local relocation assistance and SDHC notice requirements not found in state law; some SDHC portal notice requirements are stated as 'currently not in effect' pending portal creation.
